rules.title: Silence warnings at the root, not with #[allow]
rules.text: A warning is fixed where it comes from: an `#[allow(...)]` that hides one keeps the defect and deletes the evidence, so the allow has to be the last resort for a false positive the compiler cannot be told about.

judgement.question: Does this allow hide a warning the code could fix, rather than suppress an unavoidable false positive?

criteria.true: the warning points at something this code could fix instead of allowing
criteria.false: the lint is a false positive here and the comment beside it says why
